subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class bounded memory write/CRUD contract in memory-core, and what limits, identity, duplicate/consolidation, snapshot, config, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: Source inspection shows the requested capability is still missing, but adding it would create public memory-write, config, persistence, and security behavior that cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
options.body: Add an approved add/list/replace/remove or unified memory tool with hard per-store limits, usage feedback, stable identity, duplicate/consolidation behavior, secret policy, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Narrow to flush and visibility first
options.body: Continue with existing memory-flush/dreaming bounds plus UI or startup warnings while leaving general CRUD writes out of the default memory tool surface for now.

options.title: Prototype the contract outside core first
options.body: Use a memory plugin or operator-facing prototype to prove the write API and safety policy before promoting it into the default memory-core contract.

recommendation.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
recommendation.body: Add an approved add/list/replace/remove or unified memory tool with hard per-store limits, usage feedback, stable identity, duplicate/consolidation behavior, secret policy, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans product direction, public API shape, memory persistence, configuration, and security boundaries rather than one implementation file.
